correctness.rationale: For each of three two-leader orbits, decompose the q-by-q grounded Laplacian into zero-sum eigenspaces plus at most a two-dimensional block. This yields the exact three heat traces in RESULT.md, with all degrees retained from the original graph. Uniform strict signs at 1/5,67/100,1 are certified by rational Taylor bounds, delta_q<19/50 for q>=9 and e^2>7. The q->infinity differences converge to three explicit expressions, and their strict comparisons prove the limiting three-phase diagram. Bundled verify.py independently tests 480 exact matrix power-sum identities and the mathematical rational certificates; finite tests are not misused as all-q proofs.

originality.rationale: Complete pertinent same-family stationary manuscripts and primary two-leader literature were compared by mathematical implication. The heat-kernel primary work covers solving follower dynamics with given leader sets, not choosing leaders. The pointwise three-orbit horizon ranking and limiting logarithmic thresholds are not implied by the examined stationary integral or gain-dependent four-leader theorems. Equivalent unindexed mathematical statements remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible pointwise heat-trace leader-selection results may exist.

The general spectral analysis of complete bipartite grounded Laplacians is elementary and known, so novelty concerns the nontrivial strict time-dependent optimizer classification, not the block diagonalization itself.
No independent audit or exhaustive global novelty certification has been performed.

value.rationale: For the concrete task of minimizing the remaining mean squared diffusion error at a prescribed time, the theorem identifies three pairwise disjoint optimal leader designs at three positive times on every graph of an infinite natural family K_{2,q}, q>=9. The precise large-network boundaries log(phi) and log2 reveal a genuine intermediate mixed-placement regime rather than a routine scalar reweighting. The strict results are structural and not isolated numerical counterexamples. The claim deliberately stops short of an unproved complete finite-size time classification.
